subject: Subprocessor lifecycle decision & export-control clarification: EdgeTransit
messages:
From: Elena M. <elena@finsecure.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@remitco.com
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor lifecycle info & export-control question: EdgeTransit

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we evaluate Redwood for production at FinSecure, our procurement and export-control teams asked for a few clarifications about the proposed EdgeTransit subprocessor you listed during onboarding. Can you confirm the following?

- Precise role: will EdgeTransit ever persist or process customer-content tokens or only operate as an egress/POP CDN for encrypted payloads?
- Data path: which countries will see plaintext (if any) and which are strictly encrypted passthroughs?
- Export control: is EdgeTransit subject to US EAR/ITAR considerations given cross-border egress? If there are any licensed cryptographic components, please call them out.
- Evidence: we need a signed DPA addendum acknowledging the subprocessor, an attestation on export-control posture (or confirm N/A), and SOC 2 excerpt covering transient egress flows.

I've attached a short template we use for requests (edge_transit_dpa_addendum_request.pdf). Can you get back to us this week with interim mitigations if the full evidence will take longer?

Appreciate it,
Elena M.
Privacy & Procurement
FinSecure Inc.

Subject: Re: Subprocessor lifecycle info & export-control question: EdgeTransit

Jordan — quick assessment below, attaching the tech sheet we have from EdgeTransit (edge_transit_tech_sheet_v2.pdf).

Summary/Risk: MEDIUM. EdgeTransit is primarily an edge POP/CDN provider that terminates TLS at the POP to improve latency. For our integration pattern, they will only see encrypted model I/O except for a small set of metadata headers (region tag, tenant id) used for routing. They are not intended to persist customer content, but we need explicit contractual language to prohibit persistence and to mandate immediate cache eviction on request.

Export control: EdgeTransit is a US-headquartered company with EU POPs. They do not ship cryptographic software themselves, but because plaintext could be terminated in EU POPs, there is a potential cross-border export consideration for certain regulated customers. I recommend we:
- Ask EdgeTransit for an export-control self-assessment (country-of-origin of all TLS certs, SSH/key rotation policies, and any FIPS modules in their stack).
- Map any regulated customers (FinSecure flagged as sensitive) and propose tenant-scoped routing to avoid US egress if requested.

Who owns what: Compliance should sign the attestation (Naomi). Legal will draft the DPA addendum language (Marissa can drive). I can assemble the tech evidence and the controls package.

Interim mitigations we can offer immediately:
- Tenant-level encryption (customer-managed keys) so EdgeTransit never holds plaintext without explicit KMS handshake.
- IP allowlist to restrict EdgeTransit endpoints to FinSecure's expected egress ranges.
- Short TTL cache eviction (24h) and documented cache purge API, enforceable by addendum.
- Audit hooks: we can enable extra request/response tracing (obfuscated) for the account for 30 days.

ETA: I can deliver the tech sheet + proposed cache eviction clause by EOD tomorrow. Naomi, could you confirm whether Compliance will sign the export-control attestation template?

-Kim

---
Attachment: edge_transit_tech_sheet_v2.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor lifecycle info & export-control question: EdgeTransit

Elena — thanks for the note and for flagging FinSecure's requirements. Below is a consolidated response and an interim controls offer while we gather the formal attestation and SOC2 excerpt.

Short answers (summary):
- Role: EdgeTransit will function as an egress/edge POP (TLS termination at POP) and routing layer. For the integration path FinSecure reviewed, EdgeTransit will NOT persist customer model content. They will observe limited routing metadata only.
- Data path: EU POPs will service EU users by default; plaintext is only transient at the POP for the duration of routing and caching. For regulated tenants we can pin routing to EU POPs and avoid US egress.
- Export control: Preliminary review suggests no ITAR obligations for the defined workload, but because transient plaintext can occur at POPs, we will obtain an export-control self-assessment from EdgeTransit and have Compliance sign an attestation if anything material is found.

Interim controls we can provide immediately (attached as redwood_interim_controls_20280915.docx):
- Tenant-managed encryption keys (KMS integration) so EdgeTransit cannot decrypt payloads without a short-lived handshake.
- IP allowlist and dedicated edge subdomain for FinSecure traffic.
- Cache TTL of 24 hours with on-demand purge API accessible to FinSecure.
- 30-day enhanced audit/tracing for the FinSecure tenant.

Timeline:
- Tech evidence + cache clause: Kim will send by EOD today.
- Compliance export attestation: target 5 business days (Naomi owning).
- SOC2 excerpt that references transient egress flows: we can provide a SOC2-type control description within 5–7 business days; full auditor report redactions as appropriate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sign a DPA addendum with cache/eviction language and interim controls (we can use FinSecure's template as a baseline).
2) We will route FinSecure to EU-only POPs by default unless you authorize global routing.
3) Deliver export-control self-assessment from EdgeTransit and Compliance attestation within the week.

Link to the DocuSign I will send for the addendum: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/XYZ123

If this plan looks acceptable, we'll start the DocuSign flow and prioritize Naomi's review.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Manager, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

- Execute the DPA addendum using our template with the cache-eviction clause and the tenant-level KMS requirement.
- Confirm routing is EU-only for our tenant by default (no US egress).
- Provide the export-control self-assessment and Compliance attestation as soon as available — we request these within the promised 5 business days.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Once the DocuSign arrives I'll route it to Procurement and Legal for signature.

Thanks,
Elena M.
